research.researchQuestion: Can current primary filings normalize Credo's dilution burden and quantify how much concentration remains after the latest quarter?
research.summary: Primary Q1 FY2027 evidence materially narrows the dilution blocker and confirms concentration remains a major resilience risk. The filing gives current shares, diluted-share bridge, SBC expense, acquisition-related equity awards and direct-customer concentration. This is enough for Chief to replace a generic dilution unknown with sourced quantitative inputs, but not enough to declare concentration durable because end-customer identities and future insourcing behavior remain unknown.

evidence.fact: 187,951,918 ordinary shares were outstanding as of 2026-08-25; quarter-end ordinary shares were 187.768M.

Q1 FY2027 basic weighted-average shares were 186.007M and diluted weighted-average shares were 194.378M; the 8.371M incremental diluted shares came from share-based compensation awards. Another 1.406M awards were excluded as anti-dilutive.

Quarter SBC expense was $87.979M versus $35.455M a year earlier, with R&D SBC $44.999M and SG&A SBC $37.265M. SBC was approximately 18.4% of $479.003M quarterly revenue and approximately 68.0% of $129.425M net income.

DustPhotonics replacement awards added 254k RSUs; Hyperlume-related retention/replacement equity included 87k RSUs plus two 132k restricted-share awards. The filing says these awards are post-acquisition compensation recognized over vesting periods up to four years.
Direct-customer revenue concentration was 43% for Customer A and 28% for Customer B in the quarter; accounts receivable concentration was 57% and 28%, respectively.

inference: Dilution is quantitatively material but now measurable: diluted weighted-average shares exceeded basic by about 4.5%, while quarter-end/share-date counts show continued equity issuance. This should be modeled explicitly rather than left as a generic penalty.
SBC intensity is high enough that operating quality should be assessed both before and after SBC; excluding it entirely would overstate owner economics.

The top two direct customers represented 71% of quarterly revenue, so concentration remains a first-order common-mode risk even though customer labels may be manufacturing/intermediary relationships rather than final end customers.
contradictions: Exceptional revenue and net-income growth coexist with SBC that rose much faster than revenue and with extreme direct-customer concentration.
unknowns: True end-customer identities behind Customer A/B and whether concentration is diversified at the end-demand layer.
Forward equity issuance from future grants beyond already disclosed awards.
Customer insourcing/design-loss probability and contract durability.
falsifiers: Material reduction in top-two concentration without margin deterioration would weaken the concentration-risk thesis.
SBC as a percentage of revenue and diluted-share growth falling sustainably while growth remains strong would weaken the dilution concern.
research.chiefHandoff: Promote the sourced share-count/SBC bridge into the CRDO dossier; keep end-customer durability open. Do not mark ready_for_chief solely from this artifact.

research.exactGate: Fully diluted share-count roll-forward and customer/governance concentration
research.researchQuestion: Can Astera's latest 10-Q close the diluted-share roll-forward and quantify dilution/customer concentration without guessing end-customer identity?
research.summary: The June 2026 10-Q materially closes the fully diluted share-count blocker. It provides current common shares, weighted-average dilution, option/RSU/PSU overhang, a large performance-contingent customer warrant, and direct-customer concentration. Governance control remains only partially closed because the 10-Q does not reproduce the full beneficial-ownership table; the 2025 10-K remains necessary for control concentration context.

evidence.fact: 173,485,104 common shares were outstanding as of 2026-07-31.

For Q2 2026, basic weighted-average shares were 172.378M and diluted weighted-average shares were 183.340M, an incremental 10.962M potentially dilutive equivalent shares, approximately 6.4% over basic.
At 2026-06-30 Astera had 1.693M options outstanding, 9.180M RSUs outstanding, and 0.375M PSUs outstanding. Unrecognized compensation was $640.1M for RSUs and $40.3M for PSUs.

A February 2026 customer warrant permits up to 3,262,299 shares at $142.82, vesting in purchase-performance tranches. Across all warrants, 1,663,042 underlying shares were vested/exercisable and 24,722 were probable of vesting at 2026-06-30; none had been exercised by the holder. Warrant contra-revenue was $10.2M in Q2 and $12.3M for the first half.

Direct-customer revenue concentration for Q2 2026 was 29%, 25%, 15%, and 13% for Customers A-D. The filing explicitly warns that some named customers are manufacturing partners purchasing on behalf of end customers, so direct-customer percentages may not represent underlying end-customer demand.
The 2025 Form 10-K states executive officers, directors and greater-than-5% holders collectively beneficially owned about 37.9% of outstanding common stock as of the stated ownership date.

inference: The diluted-share blocker can be converted from unknown to a sourced roll-forward: current common shares plus material option/RSU/PSU and customer-warrant overhang are now quantified.
The customer warrant is economically linked to purchases, so part of dilution is paired with commercial volume rather than being pure financing dilution; Chief should preserve that distinction.
Direct-customer concentration is very high, but the filing itself cautions that manufacturing-partner labels can obscure the true end-customer map.
contradictions: Strong profitability and growth coexist with a meaningful equity-compensation/warrant overhang and concentrated commercial channels.
unknowns: Exact mapping from direct Customers A-D to ultimate hyperscale/end customers.
Current beneficial-ownership/control percentages after 2026 share issuance and vesting; the 37.9% figure is useful context but not a current-quarter ownership roll-forward.
Probability and timing of future customer-warrant tranche vesting.
falsifiers: A later proxy/13D/13G ownership set showing materially dispersed control would weaken the governance-concentration concern.
A reconciled end-customer map showing broad diversification beneath manufacturing partners would weaken the concentration concern.
research.chiefHandoff: Treat the fully diluted share-count gate as materially closed for baseline construction, subject to Chief reconciliation. Keep true end-customer mapping and refreshed governance/control ownership as narrow remaining gaps.

research.researchQuestion: Does the newest Broadcom 10-Q show a defensible post-VMware deleveraging path and remaining balance-sheet constraint?
research.summary: The newest available Q3 FY2026 10-Q materially closes the debt-normalization blocker. Debt principal fell by about $6.0B from fiscal-year-end 2025 to August 2, 2026, and carrying debt fell by about $5.7B. The company still carries roughly $61.1B aggregate indebtedness and explicitly identifies that leverage as a strategic constraint. VMware-related tax indemnity risk remains separate from ordinary debt service and should not be collapsed into the debt metric.

evidence.fact: Total debt principal outstanding was $61.079B at 2026-08-02 versus $67.120B at 2025-11-02, a $6.041B reduction. Carrying total debt was $59.419B versus $65.136B, a $5.717B reduction.
At 2026-08-02, short-term debt was $2.252B and long-term debt was $57.167B.
The filing explicitly states aggregate indebtedness of $61.079B remains substantial and can limit strategic flexibility, increase vulnerability and constrain future borrowing.
The filing separately preserves potential VMware-related tax indemnity exposure tied to the 2021 Dell spin-off and tax-free qualification; this risk is not the same as scheduled funded debt.

inference: The direction of deleveraging is clear and material: principal debt declined about 9.0% from fiscal-year-end to Q3 FY2026.
Leverage is no longer an unquantified VMware-integration unknown, but it remains a material risk factor because absolute debt is still very large.
Chief should keep VMware tax-indemnity tail risk separate from ordinary debt normalization to avoid double counting.
contradictions: Broadcom is demonstrably deleveraging while simultaneously retaining an absolute debt load large enough for the company itself to flag strategic consequences.
unknowns: Exact debt attributed economically to VMware versus other Broadcom financing once fungible cash flows/refinancings are considered.
Future refinancing cost under different rate regimes.
Magnitude/probability of VMware spin-off tax indemnity exposure.
falsifiers: A reversal to rising net debt without a corresponding high-return investment case would falsify the improving-deleveraging inference.
A definitive tax ruling eliminating VMware indemnity exposure would remove that tail risk.
research.chiefHandoff: Promote the Q3 FY2026 debt bridge into AVGO underwriting and downgrade the debt blocker from unresolved to quantified/monitor. Keep AI customer concentration as the principal remaining active gate.

research.exactGate: Backlog aging/cancellation quality and customer concentration
research.researchQuestion: Can primary filings distinguish firm backlog quality from headline backlog and show whether cancellation risk is actually low?
research.summary: Primary filings strengthen backlog quality but do not fully close the gate. Vertiv's 2025 10-K says the majority of $15.0B year-end backlog was considered firm and expected to ship within 12-18 months, while also stating orders can be cancelled or rescheduled. The Q2 2026 10-Q continues to flag unpredictable order placement/cancellation, failure to realize backlog, and large-customer contract leverage as material risks. This supports a 'high-quality but not irrevocable' backlog classification rather than treating the full backlog as guaranteed revenue.

evidence.fact: At 2025-12-31 Vertiv reported $15.0B estimated backlog versus $7.2B a year earlier; the majority was considered firm and expected to ship within 12-18 months, but orders may be cancelled or rescheduled by customers.

The Q2 2026 10-Q continues to list unpredictable placement/cancellation of customer orders, failure to realize expected sales from backlog, shifts in customer technology spending, and reduced leverage with large customers as explicit risks.

Q2 2026 net sales were $3.274B, up 24.1% year over year, while the company disclosed minor timing shifts from supply-chain congestion and multi-phased project execution as deployments scale in size and complexity.

At 2026-06-30 Vertiv had $2.811B cash, $0.300B short-term investments and $2.484B revolver availability; it had repaid its prior term loan in full in March 2026 and released the associated guarantees/liens.

inference: The backlog should not be haircut as if it were merely soft pipeline: management classifies the majority as firm and near-to-medium-term. However, it also should not be valued as an unconditional receivable because cancellation/rescheduling and project-timing risks are explicit.
Balance-sheet strengthening reduces the risk that backlog execution is constrained by financing capacity; the remaining gate is commercial concentration/conversion quality rather than liquidity.
Project complexity and phased deployments can move revenue timing without necessarily indicating demand destruction, so future misses should be decomposed into cancellation versus timing/slippage.
contradictions: Management describes most backlog as firm while simultaneously preserving explicit cancellation/rescheduling and technology-spending risks; both facts must remain visible.
unknowns: Current quarter-end backlog amount and age buckets were not found in the primary sources reviewed in this pass.
Cancellation rate history and concentration by top customer are not quantified in the cited filings.
Share of backlog tied to hyperscalers versus broader colocation/enterprise demand remains unresolved.
falsifiers: A disclosed material rise in cancellations, aging beyond expected shipment windows, or backlog-to-revenue conversion deterioration would weaken the backlog-quality inference.
A customer-level disclosure showing extreme hyperscaler concentration would strengthen concentration risk.
research.chiefHandoff: Retain backlog as a positive operating signal but classify it as firm-yet-cancellable. Seek current backlog amount, cancellation history and customer concentration before marking VRT ready_for_chief.

gatesMateriallyClosedOrNarrowed: CRDO SBC/dilution is now quantitatively normalized; concentration durability remains open.
ALAB fully diluted share-count roll-forward is materially closed; end-customer mapping and refreshed ownership/control remain open.
AVGO VMware-era debt/deleveraging is quantitatively normalized; AI customer concentration remains open.
VRT backlog quality is better characterized as majority-firm but cancellable; current aging/cancellation/customer-concentration metrics remain open.
batchImpact.reasoning: ALAB and AVGO each had one named quantitative blocker materially closed by fresh primary evidence, leaving narrower independent gates. CRDO still has extreme concentration durability unresolved; VRT still lacks current backlog aging/cancellation/customer concentration.
